title: Border lace shawl
subtitle: A top-down fingering triangle in garter with a 10-row lace border at the cast-off edge.
excerpt: A top-down triangular shawl in fingering-weight wool with a plain garter body and a 10-row horseshoe lace border worked across all stitches immediately before the cast-off. The lace border is the entire pattern focus. Wingspan 170 cm, centre-back depth 80 cm. About 360 g of fingering yarn.
sourceNotes: Border lace on a garter-body triangle shawl is a Victorian convention. The horseshoe lace used for the border appears in Weldon's Practical Knitter, 5th series (1890), §Lace Stitches. Top-down construction follows Elizabeth Zimmermann, Knitting Without Tears (1971).

knitting.gaugeText: 24 sts × 48 rows = 10 × 10 cm in garter stitch on 3.75 mm needles, blocked.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Wingspan 170 cm. Centre-back depth 80 cm. Blocked.

glossaryTerms.definition: A small strip of garter stitch worked on a few stitches, rotated and picked up to form the centre-back starting point of a top-down triangle shawl.

content.text: A top-down fingering triangle with a plain garter body and a horseshoe lace border across the final 10 RS rows. Wingspan 170 cm, depth 80 cm.

The body is entirely plain garter stitch and the 4-stitch-per-RS-row spine increases. The horseshoe lace border is introduced only for the final 10 RS rows (just 5 pattern repeats), so there is no sustained lace knitting for most of the shawl. Begins with a
garter tab
. Budget about 360 g (about 1,440 m / 1,570 yards) of fingering wool.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: About 360 g (1,440 m / 1,570 yards) of fingering-weight yarn

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 3.75 mm (UK 9 / US 5) circular needle, 100 cm or longer

items.name: Tapestry needle, scissors, blocking mat, pins

content.text: Gauge

24 stitches and 48 rows to 10 cm over garter stitch on 3.75 mm needles, blocked. At gauge, 170 cm wingspan requires approximately 204 RS rows total; the final 10 are lace border rows (approximately 2.5 cm of depth). If your blocked gauge reads 26 stitches per 10 cm, the wingspan at 204 RS rows will be approximately 157 cm; add 18 plain garter RS rows to compensate.
Stitches used
Pattern
Garter tab
Work the garter tab: 3 sts on waste yarn, 6 garter rows, pick up 9 sts. Place markers: after st 1, after st 5 (centre), before st 9.
Garter body
RS row: k1, yo, SM, yo, k to centre marker, yo, SM, yo, k to last st, yo, k1. WS row: k all sts. Continue for 194 RS rows (to approximately 167 cm wingspan at gauge).
Horseshoe lace border (10 RS rows)

Replace the plain garter body stitches with horseshoe lace on the final 10 RS rows. Continue the 4-stitch spine increases as normal throughout. Horseshoe lace RS row (6 sts): k2tog, yo, k2, yo, ssk. WS rows: k all sts.
Bind off
Work Jeny's surprisingly stretchy bind-off after the final lace RS row.
Stitch count check-ins
After 100 RS rows: 9 + 400 = 409 stitches. Wingspan approximately 86 cm.
At the start of lace border (after 194 RS rows): 9 + 776 = 785 stitches. Wingspan approximately 167 cm. The horseshoe repeat must divide evenly into each wing (each wing ≈ 390 sts ÷ 6 = 65 repeats).
Common faults

Horseshoe repeat doesn't divide evenly into wing stitch count: the stitch count at the border start is not a multiple of 6. Add or subtract 1 to 3 plain garter RS rows to reach the nearest multiple of 6 before starting the lace section.
Blocking
Wet-block to wingspan 170 cm. Pin the horseshoe lace border to open the arches. The garter body pinned first to its depth of 78 cm, then the lace border pinned as the outermost 2 cm.
Care
Hand wash in cool water, lay flat to dry. Re-block the lace border when the arches close after wearing.
What to try next
Deepen the lace border to 30 RS rows for a more pronounced lace section. At 30 rows the border adds about 7.5 cm of depth and becomes the visual centrepiece of the shawl.
